title: School Improvement Starts Here: Behaviour, Attention, Participation, and Memory 2025
author: Adam Boxer
summary: Adam Boxer offers a deliberately sequenced starting point for school improvement, built around three questions leaders should investigate in strict priority order. First: is there disruption-free learning in almost every lesson? Behaviour comes first, he argues, because nothing else is possible in a school where poor behaviour robs students of learning time and destroys staff morale. Once that is largely secured, the second question is whether every student is paying attention and participating, addressed through name-at-end questioning and a habit of asking every student at least one question per lesson, eventually building toward mini-whiteboard use in nearly every lesson. The third and final question is whether the school has a long-term memory strategy, since lessons without a systematic retrieval-practice programme deliver little lasting value however well they are taught. Boxer argues these three issues -- behaviour, attention and participation, memory -- are shared by every school regardless of context, and should be tackled in that order before anything else.
points: Boxer's ordering argument is the piece's spine: behaviour must come first because it is a precondition for everything else, not because it is more important in the abstract -- "nothing is possible in a school where behaviour is poor."

His attention-and-participation fix is concrete and low-cost: name-at-end questioning (question, pause, name) plus a personal habit of asking every student at least one question every lesson, without needing a tally system.
Mini-whiteboards are positioned as the natural endpoint of the attention-and-participation phase, to be rolled out toward near-universal use once questioning habits are established.

The long-term memory strategy question is framed as the final, not first, priority -- Boxer's implicit critique of schools that jump straight to retrieval-practice initiatives while behaviour and attention remain unresolved.
quotes: Behaviour comes first because, well, it has to come first. Nothing is possible in a school where behaviour is poor.
Poor behaviour is a lead weight on school improvement, and there is little point focusing on anything else until it is fixed.
This strategy, simply called Name at End questioning, communicates that all students have to be listening to the question, as they do not know who it will go to.
The most powerful of these strategies is the use of mini-whiteboards, and leaders should quickly move towards a target of mini-whiteboards being used in almost every lesson.
However good your lessons are, without a long term memory strategy, they are worth very little. Humans forget things, and they forget things fast.
The issues of behaviour, attention, participation and memory are shared by all schools and transcend the idiosyncrasies that make schools such varied and fascinating places to visit and work in.
